title: Harness to-do: decisions before we build
intro:
Plans for your 23 items plus the open items from the ayepi session. The full plan is in **docs/plans/todo-2026-11-18.md**, with findings, files and order. The recommended options are marked. Blocking questions shape the first phases.

**Read first:** "You there?" failed because every database fn was held by a pending system review, and the hub never told the model why. It also said those fns were in its tools when they weren't. Then Retry kept the whole failed turn in the transcript.

questions.question: What order should we build these in?
questions.why: There are 23 items, 5 of them library work in aits or ayepi. The plan doc proposes: 1 chat fixes, 2 admin polish, 3 prompt format, 4 system pages, 5 aits work, 6 A/B and SSO.

options.label: As the plan doc orders them
options.description: Chat fixes first: they are what made "You there?" fail.

options.label: Move SSO earlier
options.description: Do it if you need other people signing in soon.

options.label: Move the aits decide/crawl work earlier
options.description: Do it if context_crawl is the priority.

questions.question: How should the build run?
questions.why: Your note says you orchestrate agents from the main session.

options.label: One workflow per phase
options.description: It uses need() guards, and I check, review and commit after each phase.

options.label: Agents per item, run by hand
options.description: Smaller steps, and you see more often.

questions.question: When a fn is unavailable, what does the model hear?
questions.why: Every database fn was held by a pending system review. load_fns said only "unavailable now", and fns_search hid them entirely. So the model never knew why, and looped 24 times.

options.label: Pass the reason everywhere
options.description: Refusals carry availability.detail ("waits for an admin to approve it"), and fns_search returns unavailable hits as available:false with the reason.

options.label: Fix the refusal text only
options.description: fns_search keeps hiding them.

questions.question: Context that "brings" fns: what does the render say?
questions.why: The context render said the database fns were "in your tools now". They were not.

options.label: List only what was added, name the held ones
options.description: For example: "held for admin review: database/create_table, …".

options.label: Drop the fns line
options.description: Simpler, but the model learns less.

questions.question: What should Retry undo?
questions.why: Retry marked the turn undone, but the transcript and the loaded tools and context stayed. The retry saw the whole failed turn (182k chars) and repeated it. The note even said "It had changed nothing."

options.label: A true redo
options.description: Trim the transcript and put back the session tools and context to before the turn. Continue becomes the gentle option.

options.label: Keep history, add a note
options.description: Tell the model the previous attempt was discarded.

questions.question: How do we stop a looping agent?
questions.why: Each iteration had some "successful" call, so the tool-failure guard never fired.

options.label: A hub no-progress guard
options.description: When the same refused or empty call repeats 3 times, the hub tells the model to stop and say what blocks it.

questions.question: Should the chat show the person when a turn hits a held system?
questions.why: You had no idea the database changes were waiting for review.

options.label: Yes: a banner with a link to the review
options.description: "database has changes waiting for review".

options.label: No, leave it to the model to say

questions.question: Should we investigate the suggestions now?
questions.why: web/guide, search, read and crawl scored about 0.98 for every message, including "track tasks". The embedder or the scoring looks broken.

questions.question: After max-iterations or cancel, what is Continue?
questions.why: Today the only option is Retry, which wipes the turn.

options.label: A new follow-up turn
options.description: It continues the transcript with a fresh step budget and a short hub note ("You ran out of steps; finish or say what blocks you").

options.label: Resume the same run
options.description: The step counter is reset.

questions.question: Should Retry (now the destructive option) ask first?

options.label: Only when the turn changed something

questions.question: How should the reasoning blocks be merged?
questions.why: Decided says reasoning, calls and content keep the model's exact order. "You there?" showed up to 24 Thinking blocks per turn.

options.label: One block per stretch before the answer text
options.description: "Thinking · N steps", with steps in order, each marked by the call it preceded.

options.label: One block per turn, at the top
Merge only reasoning pieces that sit next to each other

questions.question: How should a tab strip that overflows behave (the JSON tab was hidden)?
questions.why: The fix goes in UiTabs, so every tab strip gets it.

options.label: Mouse wheel scrolls it sideways, plus edge arrows
options.description: The selected tab stays in view.

options.label: Wrap the tabs onto two lines

questions.question: The draggable side panel width: shared or per panel?
questions.why: The width is remembered per device. Minimum 360px, maximum about 60% of the screen, double-click resets it.

options.label: One width for every chat panel
options.description: Run, LLM call, tree and resource panels all share it.

questions.question: Clickable fn pills: how should the modal work?
questions.why: Fn names show as dead text in about 15 places (GrantsView "May call", review lists, the LLM call's tools, approvals…).

options.label: One app-wide modal bound to ?fn=
options.description: Every page that opens a fn becomes shareable.

options.label: Each pill opens its own modal

questions.question: What text does a pill show?

options.label: The friendly label, with the qualified name on hover

questions.question: A/B compare: what about fns that write?
questions.why: N variants doing writes would act N times.

options.label: Writes allowed, each approved per variant
Only the chosen variant replays its writes

questions.question: A/B compare: what can vary between variants?

options.label: Model, context mode / contextor and fn mode
Any session setting, including the system prompt

questions.question: A/B compare: how many variants, and what budget?
questions.why: Spend multiplies with each variant.

options.label: Up to 4, each reserved against the turn budget up front

questions.question: The Claude page: how should it look?
questions.why: Thinking is raw <details> and tool input is raw JSON. The send bug is a shared race and gets fixed either way.

options.label: Rebuild it from the chat's own components
options.description: It looks and acts like the chat.

questions.question: How does a system add pages?
questions.why: The Claude UI is hardcoded in packages/web, with its nav item always shown. Widgets and database bits are hardcoded too. The SDK client() has no pages today.

options.label: A declared pages entry in the contract plus the client() component
options.description: Reviewed at go-live, can be added at runtime, shown only while the system is live.

options.label: Client-only registration
options.description: Nothing in the contract.

questions.question: What URL shape should system pages use?

options.label: /s/<system>/<page>
options.description: Can't collide with hub routes.

questions.question: Which systems move now?
questions.why: Widgets are wired into run cards, so they need a result-renderer slot.

options.label: Claude now, widgets in the next build

questions.question: Where is single-instance declared?
questions.why: system.json already has instances: one|many, but it only blocks a second install and never reaches the UI.

options.label: system.json, and paired systems send it in hello
options.description: One source, as for name and version.

options.label: In the contract, with system.json checked against it

questions.question: A many system with only one instance connected: what does the UI show?

options.label: The fleet UI anyway
options.description: Predictable.

options.label: Collapse to the simple view until a second instance appears

questions.question: Is this split right?
questions.why: one: code, embedder, google-calendar, input, random, template, web, widgets. many: api, claude, database, fs, mcp.

questions.question: With the graph moved under Admin, should the hub graph endpoint become admin-only too?
questions.why: The endpoint already filters to what the person may see, and the chat's hub/graph uses it.

options.label: UI only; the endpoint and the fn stay

questions.question: Graph search with ListSearch: who maps the query?

options.label: The hub graph endpoint takes ListQuery filters
options.description: One query language, and the model's hub/graph gets the same filters.

questions.question: Pending tab: approve per item?
questions.why: The new tab gets a risk summary first, then each section drawn with its own tab's component (fn facts, type diff, context word diff, grants delta), and the raw diff behind a toggle.

options.label: Per-item approve or decline
options.description: Needs hub support; matches the review's per-item switches.

questions.question: Which counts go on the system cards?
questions.why: Counted in SQL, which also fixes the current load-every-fn on each list.

options.label: fns, context, types, instances (when 2+), plus pending and refusals as warning badges

questions.question: What does "toggle all fns" do?
questions.why: It also turns off mentions and hooks, and its text will say so.

options.label: A master switch, like the Context tab
options.description: Each fn keeps its own setting underneath.

options.label: A bulk action that rewrites every fn's switch

questions.question: How do we make every fn have an example?
questions.why: Kind-derived fns (queries, table fns, forms, API, MCP, agents) get none today. KindDescription gets examples.

options.label: Build error for static fns; examples required in KindDescription

questions.question: Agent fns (hub/llm), where examples can't be derived: what then?

options.label: The author writes one at creation; the agent builder asks for it

questions.question: Should the XML card format be used beyond suggestions?
questions.why: Suggested fns and context become <suggested_fns><fn name mode>…</fn></suggested_fns>, with instructions and examples inside in static mode.

options.label: Yes: the same XML for every fn and context card in the prompt
options.description: One format.

questions.question: Full static-mode cards in every user message add up in the transcript. What should older messages keep?

options.label: Full detail on the latest message, names only on older ones

questions.question: Which system changes does the model hear about?
questions.why: The first turn lists every available system with its description (stable, so it caches). Later changes go as <systems_changed> XML in the user message.

options.label: All changes, including disconnects and admin disables
options.description: Otherwise the model calls dead fns.

options.label: Only your own toggles, as literally asked

questions.question: Context page hybrid search: how do the filters combine with text?
questions.why: Today the context list searches in memory, which breaks the "search in the database" rule. Other lists do the same; I'll audit them all.

options.label: Filters go into the search query, run in the database
Search returns names, then the list filters them
options.description: Lossy, capped at 100 names.

questions.question: Should context search also cover content sections, or only the indexed item text?

options.label: Also content sections
options.description: Better recall on long items, more to index.

questions.question: Fold "embedders" into system-provided aeye providers?
questions.why: Systems can already bring aeye providers (chat + embed). Embedders are a parallel concept.

options.label: Yes: an embedder is a provider model with the embedding capability
options.description: One source of truth; image embeddings come for free.

questions.question: Which models does a system provider expose?

options.label: Live listModels, limited to the reviewed set
options.description: New models wait for review.

questions.question: Two kinds of "decision model": what do we do?
questions.why: Today suggestions use a chat model asked for JSON. Nothing calls ai.decide.

options.label: A new decide role for real decision models
options.description: Suggestions keep their chat-model picker.

questions.question: How do we know an Ollama model can decide?
questions.why: Ollama doesn't document a capability flag for System One.

options.label: From /api/show capabilities if present, else an admin flag on the provider

questions.question: Ollama takes at most 64 questions and 64 KiB per call, but you asked for 256 per call. How do we handle it?

options.label: aeye splits on its own and merges answers and usage
options.description: Callers ask for 256.

options.label: A ModelInfo.maxQuestions field that callers respect

questions.question: context_crawl: which links are conditional?
questions.why: Context has imports (always pulled), choices ({to, when ≤200 chars}), and soft links (related, next, parent) with no condition.

options.label: Only choices: they carry an explicit when
Choices plus soft links, using the target's description as the condition

questions.question: context_crawl: what shape do the questions take?

options.label: One yes/no question per link
options.description: Independent and calibrated; up to 256 per call.

options.label: One choice per node among its options
options.description: Picks only one.

questions.question: context_crawl: what does it return?

options.label: Loads into the session like load_context, returns a summary
options.description: Loaded, skipped, stop reason.

options.label: Returns the content inline, without loading

questions.question: context_crawl: the keep threshold?

options.label: An admin setting on the decide role

questions.question: aeye image embeddings: what request shape?
questions.why: Providers: Bedrock (Titan Multimodal, Cohere v3/v4, Nova), Replicate CLIP, OpenRouter where its API takes images. OpenAI has none.

questions.question: Harness index: one vector space or two?
questions.why: A text query only finds images in the same model's space. Changing models means re-indexing.

options.label: A second vector space for images, keyed by embedder
options.description: Keeps EmbeddingGemma's text quality.

options.label: One multimodal pair for everything
options.description: Replaces EmbeddingGemma.

questions.question: SSO: which providers?
questions.why: ayepi has no OIDC. Plan: lift the OAuth client from @ayepi/mcp into @ayepi/auth, then add OIDC JWKS verification there.

options.label: Generic OIDC only
options.description: Presets pre-fill Google, Microsoft Entra, Okta and Auth0.

options.label: OIDC plus GitHub
options.description: GitHub is OAuth-only and needs special code.

questions.question: SSO: who may sign in the first time?
questions.why: This is the main security setting.

options.label: Auto-create as member when the email domain is allowed
Invited only: an admin adds the email first

questions.question: SSO: link a sign-in to an existing user?
questions.why: Without a verified-email check, a provider with unverified emails can take over an account.

options.label: Link on a matching email only when email_verified is true
Always ask for the password first

questions.question: SSO: where do roles come from?

options.label: Claims (groups/roles) map to admin, member and groups, re-synced each sign-in
options.description: Locked so the last admin can't be demoted.

options.label: Set by hand in the hub

questions.question: Passwords once SSO is on?

options.label: Only the bootstrap admin keeps one (break-glass); everyone else uses SSO

questions.question: Where does the SSO config live?

options.label: The database plus Admin › People › Sign-in, with the secret sealed

questions.question: Members become real users. Do the member-facing pages get a pass in this batch?
questions.why: Admin-only reads (runs, model calls, systems) turn into empty or 403 pages for members, and members approve their own writes by default.

questions.header: From the other session (ayepi docs pass)
questions.question: Should gin types get real JSON shapes?
questions.why: They are {} today: honest but unhelpful. A .meta() or override on the z.custom schemas in gin.ts would fix it.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Model-facing tool schemas are built from these.

questions.header: From the other session (ayepi docs pass)
questions.question: Should we merge identical helpers that have different generated names?
questions.why: The docs are correct, just noisier.

questions.header: From the other session (ayepi docs pass)
questions.question: Should we fix the MCP toInputSchema string placeholder (packages/mcp/src/index.ts)?

questions.header: From the other session (ayepi docs pass)
questions.question: Strict JSON Schema 2020-12 validation?
questions.why: Only Ajv 6 is available, and it can't check 2020-12.

options.label: Add Ajv 2020 as a dev dependency and validate in tests
Keep the ref and placeholder scans

questions.header: From the other session (ayepi docs pass)
questions.question: When should the uncommitted ayepi changes be committed?
questions.why: ayepi publishes on commit. Harness still uses the local linked branches.

options.label: Batch them with the ayepi OIDC work
options.description: One release.

options.label: Hold until you signal the switch to published
